product.schneider-towerat260.summary: The largest-disk Tower AT among the studied 2xx models, with a documented 12.5 MHz EGA specimen.
product.schneider-towerat260.history: Tower AT 260 extended the compact range with a 60 MB disk, above the 220 and 240. The range overview and an owner's testimony distinguish this variant from the 10 MHz configurations: a 260 with EGA at 12.5 MHz exists. Preserved sources do not securely establish its first sale date or initial price.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.c: Clock speed must be tied to the variant. Citronalco corrected his initial 12 MHz description to 12.5 MHz for his EGA 260; Jungsi also lists 12.5 MHz, 60 MB and a 1.44 MB floppy drive. This speed is not attributed to the whole family.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.f: An owner-linked dump lead exists for the 260. Citronalco posted BIOS 1.05A in two 32 KiB EPROMs. The library holds a MAME-sourced pair with that version, but it has not been compared with the forum ZIP: public download returned 403.
product.schneider-towerat260.warning: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach remains unvalidated.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.v: Sources and file hashes have been checked. BluMach a1b0125d has no dedicated entry for this model; MAME groups Tower AT 2xx machines as not working. Booting has not been tested.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.l: The complete machine still needs validation. Board, BIOS pair and video ROM must be identified, then POST, memory, keyboard, RTC, disks and ports tested before usable emulation can be claimed.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.b: A shared case does not guarantee the same board. The preserved manual covers 201/202/220; its architecture guides research, but schematics and revisions for this variant still need comparison.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.m: Schneider, Service Manual Tower AT 201/202/220, Ident-Nr. 44657, 03/1989: cover and CPU/memory diagrams reviewed; PDF preserved.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.r: Happy Computer 11/1988, M. Ohnesorg/rz, Rechengiganten zu Niedrigpreisen, pp. 97–98 and 101: review of a Tower AT without a hard disk, with no commercial suffix identified.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.m: Happy Computer 05/1989, Sammlerstück, p. 18: 220 Mega edition, equipment, prices and announced production run; scan and transcription preserved.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.o: Citronalco, VzEkC, posts 40 and 42 of 26 March 2016: Tower AT 260 with EGA, 12.5 MHz and BIOS 1.05A in two 27256 EPROMs. Attachment located; public download blocked.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.r: Jungsi, Schneider VGA AT System 40: range overview and approximate chronology; not a substitute for a manual covering each revision.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.m: MAME, at.cpp: towerat2xx sets, variant provenance and unresolved EGA pairings. Files are preserved in the library; their presence does not prove universal compatibility.
product.schneider-towerat260.technical.c: BluMach a1b0125d, inspected and preserved machine table: no dedicated Tower AT entry.
